autoHaptics.blurb: Derive haptic feedback from the game's speaker audio for titles that send no native HD-haptic data (e.g. Ghost of Tsushima on Linux + Steam).

off.label: Off
off.hint: Default. Native haptics only (channels 2 + 3 of the USB audio stream).

fallback.label: Fallback
fallback.hint: Derived haptic fires only when the game has been silent on the native haptic path for ~1 s. Preserves native HD haptics (Spider-Man Remastered, etc.) while filling in for games that send no haptic data (Ghost of Tsushima on Linux, etc.).

mix.label: Mix
mix.hint: Always add derived haptic on top of native, soft-clipped together. Best for adding more body to games with weak native haptics.

replace.label: Replace
replace.hint: Always use derived; discard native completely. Uniform feel across all games regardless of what they send.

behavior.hint: Polling rate, controller mode, LED behavior, inactive disconnect — most users never change these.

lightbar.blurb: Pick the lightbar mode and four favorite colors. Also editable on the OLED; HOST hands the LED to the game.

remap.blurb: Reassign any controller button to another. The map is stored on the dongle, so it works in every game and on every OS with no extra software. Changes are written and saved the moment you click Apply.
remap.unsupported: The connected firmware doesn't support button remapping. Update to the latest OLED Edition firmware on the Flash tab.
remap.connectHint: Connect a device to edit button remapping.
remap.applied: Remapping applied and saved to the dongle.
remap.applyTitle: Write the remap table to the dongle and persist it (report 0xF6)
remap.revertTitle: Discard edits and restore the dongle's current remapping
remap.resetTitle: Clear all remapping (identity) — then click Apply
remap.verifyFailed: Remap write could not be verified — the device did not confirm the change.
remap.diagramHint: Click a button on the controller to set its remap.

slots.blurb: Bond up to four DualSenses. The active slot reconnects on boot.

preview.blurb: Live emulation of the firmware's 10 OLED screens — close to what the physical Pico-OLED-1.3 shows but not byte-perfect. Auto-cycles every 4 s with mock data when no controller is connected. With a controller connected (click Connect above), data is live. Share #preview to land Discord viewers directly on this view.
preview.liveDemoBanner: Live demo — connect a controller for real values.
preview.firmwareNote: Trigger haptics only fire if your dongle is running MarcelineVPQ/DS5Dongle-OLED-Edition firmware.
preview.mockNote: Mock values — Chrome WebHID can't expose this report on a stock DualSense descriptor. See the HID diagnostic for evidence.
preview.key1Title: KEY1 — back / cycle preset on Trigger Test / cycle mode on Lightbar

validation.hapticsGain: Haptics gain must be between 1.0 and 2.0
validation.speakerVolume: Speaker volume must be between -100 dB and 0 dB
validation.inactiveTime: Inactive time must be between 5 and 60 minutes
validation.pollingRateMode: Polling rate mode must be 0, 1, or 2
validation.audioBufferLength: Audio buffer length must be between 16 and 128
validation.autoHapticsEnable: Auto Haptics mode must be 0 (Off), 1 (Fallback), 2 (Mix), or 3 (Replace)
validation.autoHapticsGain: Auto Haptics gain must be between 0 % and 200 %
validation.autoHapticsLowpass: Auto Haptics LP must be 0-3 (80/160/250/400 Hz)

flash.blurb: Push a .uf2 firmware image to the Pico over WebUSB — no picotool, no drag-and-drop. Use this to upgrade or reflash without leaving the browser. Powered by piersfinlayson/picoflash.
flash.webusbUnavailable: WebUSB isn't available in this browser. Use Chrome, Edge, Vivaldi, Brave, or Opera.
flash.step1Hint: Use the latest release bundled with this site, or load a local build (build/ds5-bridge-oled.uf2).
flash.step2Title: 2. Put the Pico in BOOTSEL and connect
flash.step2Hint: Hold the BOOTSEL button while plugging in USB. The Pico will appear as a removable drive named “RP2350” (Linux / macOS) or “RPI-RP2” (Windows) — that's expected; you don't need to open or interact with it. Then click “Connect to Pico” below and authorize the device when the browser prompts. Linux users: a one-time udev rule is needed for WebUSB permission — see “Driver / permission setup” at the bottom of this page.
flash.step3Hint: Erases the flash region, writes the new firmware, and reboots the Pico. Takes a few seconds.
flash.rebootTitle: Reboot the Pico out of BOOTSEL into application mode
flash.done: Done — Pico is rebooting into the new firmware.
flash.trustWarning: You're about to write firmware that will run with USB-device privileges on any host this dongle plugs into. Only flash UF2 files from sources you trust.
flash.driverHelpLinux: Linux requires a one-time udev rule so non-root users can access the Pico's BOOTSEL interface. Paste this in a terminal:
flash.driverHelpWindows: Windows needs the WinUSB driver assigned to the BOOTSEL interface. Use
flash.driverHelpMac: macOS usually works without any setup. If WebUSB can't see the Pico, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and grant the browser USB device access, then retry.

empty.body: It connects automatically. Needs OLED Edition firmware v0.8 or newer.

bar.saved: All changes saved on the dongle.

settings.usbHint: These take effect after Reconnect USB (the PC sees the dongle unplug and replug).
settings.speakerLevelSub: 0 = unchanged; above 0 boosts and can clip

lightbar.hint: While charging, the dongle shows an amber pulse in every mode.

slots.title: Pairing slots
slots.hint: Each slot remembers one controller. Switching disconnects the current controller; press PS on the one in the new slot. To pair a new controller into an empty slot, switch to it and hold Create + PS.

triggers.title: Adaptive trigger test
triggers.hint: Pick an effect, then pull L2 and R2. Games override this as soon as they send their own trigger effects.

diag.title: Audio pipeline counters
diag.core1Frozen: Core1 stopped: the audio path is dead until the dongle restarts.

firmware.updatesSoon: Automatic firmware updates are coming in the next build.
firmware.rebooting: Restarting… press PS on the controller once it's back.
firmware.bootsel: The dongle is now an RP2350 drive. Copy a .uf2 onto it, or unplug it to cancel.
firmware.resetDone: Settings reset to defaults and saved.
firmware.resetHint: Factory reset restores default settings. Pairings and button remaps are kept.
firmware.updateHint: The dongle restarts into its bootloader, gets flashed and restarts on its own. Keep it plugged in; press PS on the controller afterwards.
